title: Provision IAM Policy
scenario: Your platform team needs IAM Policy for a scoped permission set. Write a reusable Terraform configuration that provisions it, drives every input through variables, applies the standard tags, and exports the operational identifiers.
constraints: Create exactly one resource of type aws_iam_policy.
All configurable values must come from variables declared in variables.tf.
Code must pass terraform fmt conventions (2-space indents, trailing newline, no tabs).
Tag the resource with Project, Environment and ManagedBy = "terraform".

focus.title: Complete the aws_iam_policy resource
focus.todo: Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_iam_policy.

hints.why: IAM is the main authorization boundary in AWS. Least-privilege policies prevent one compromised workload from becoming an account-wide incident.
hints.what: Complete the marked TODO in `main.tf`. Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_iam_policy. Use the visible constraints as your checklist before you run the tests.
hints.when: Create IAM resources when a workload or operator needs narrowly scoped permissions, and prefer roles and temporary credentials over long-lived keys.
hints.how: Open `main.tf` and work inside the single TODO region. Change one requirement at a time: add the named block, argument or reference, then run the tests. When a check fails, match its wording to the constraints and fix only the block it names.
